subject: pathology
title: Acute and Chronic Pancreatitis, Fat Necrosis, Pseudocysts, and Pancreatic Cancer CA 19-9

steps.tx: Acute pancreatitis autodigests itself when trypsin activates prematurely inside acinar cells from gallstone obstruction or alcohol, enzymes digesting pancreas and peripancreatic fat into haemorrhagic necrosis. Premature activation ignites **acute pancreatitis, interstitial versus necrotising**. Necrotising disease, unlike the oedematous form, can become infected after the second week and then needs drainage.
steps.say: Trypsin switched on inside the gland digests pancreas and fat; gallstones and alcohol light most fires.

vis.caption: Acute pancreatitis pathophysiology from premature enzyme activation to necrosis.

steps.tx: Fat necrosis saponifies peripancreatic and omental fat into chalky white deposits as lipases free fatty acids that bind calcium, occasionally hypocalcaemia marking severe disease prognostically. Those chalk deposits are **fat necrosis with saponification in acute pancreatitis**. A corrected calcium below 8 mg per decilitre on day two is one of the classic Ranson severity signs.
steps.say: Chalky fat necrosis is lipase handwriting; falling calcium beside it grades severity grimly.

nodes.label: Fatty acids bind calcium into soaps

steps.tx: Diagnosis needs two of characteristic epigastric pain radiating to back, amylase or lipase tripled, and imaging inflammation, lipase outperforming amylase in specificity and window. Severity scores follow: **acute pancreatitis diagnostic criteria (revised Atlanta)**. Lipase stays raised for 8 to 14 days, so it still helps when a patient arrives several days after pain began.
steps.say: Pain, tripled lipase, imaging: any two diagnose pancreatitis; lipase beats amylase on both counts.

steps.tx: Chronic pancreatitis fibroses gland irreversibly chiefly from alcohol, calcifying ducts, destroying exocrine then endocrine function into steatorrhoea and diabetes with chronic pain. That fibrotic endpoint is **chronic calcifying pancreatitis**. Plain imaging may show calcification scattered along the main duct, and enzyme replacement is judged by weight gain and stool fat, not pain alone.
steps.say: Alcohol calcifies and fibroses the pancreas until enzymes and insulin both fail behind chronic pain.

vis.caption: Chronic pancreatitis pathology with fibrosis, calcification, and duct distortion.

steps.tx: Pancreatic pseudocysts wall off enzyme rich fluid collections after four weeks without epithelial lining, persisting, infecting, rupturing, or compressing until drainage selected by anatomy and symptoms. The unlined collection is the **pancreatic pseudocyst of pancreatitis**. A collection under four weeks old has no mature wall, so early drainage usually fails and observation is safer.
steps.say: Pseudocysts have walls of scar, not epithelium; size alone never mandates drainage, symptoms do.

steps.tx: Pancreatic adenocarcinoma of ductal origin, KRAS almost universal, hides retroperitoneally until weight loss, pain, painless jaundice from head tumours, new diabetes, or migratory thrombosis declares advanced disease. Its silence defines **pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma presentation**. A double duct sign, both bile and pancreatic ducts dilated on imaging, points strongly to a periampullary tumour.
steps.say: Painless jaundice, weight loss, new diabetes in an older adult: pancreatic head cancer until CT acquits it.

vis.caption: Pancreatic cancer signs including Courvoisier gallbladder and weight loss.

steps.tx: CA 19-9, a Lewis antigen glycan, rises in pancreatic cancer yet also in cholestasis and cholangitis and never in Lewis negative patients, serving prognosis and monitoring rather than screening. That caveat defines **CA 19-9 interpretation in pancreatic cancer**. Roughly 5 to 10 percent of people are Lewis negative and cannot secrete it at all, however advanced their cancer becomes.
steps.say: CA 19-9 monitors known pancreatic cancer; jaundice alone raises it and Lewis negative patients never make it.

steps.tx: Trousseau migratory thrombophlebitis returns as pancreatic cancer's paraneoplastic flag beside depression and new diabetes, while Courvoisier palpable gallbladder separates malignant from stone obstruction classically. Those bedside flags are **pancreatic cancer clinical signatures, Trousseau and Courvoisier**. Courvoisier gallbladder is palpable and nontender; a stone scarred gallbladder usually cannot distend enough to be felt.
steps.say: Migratory clots, new diabetes, and a palpable painless gallbladder triangulate pancreatic cancer at the bedside.
